rows.recordSays: THIS ARCHIVE WITHDRAWS ITS OWN INFERENCE. From Orazio naming two sons Domenico, naming custom suggested his father was a Domenico Arena. Two Orazio Arena births at Scilla now say otherwise: act 10 of 1821 gives him a father GIUSEPPE (and the tree's own year, 1821, exactly), and act 1 of 1833 gives a different Orazio a father BONAVENTURA. Neither is a Domenico. The mistake was not the custom but the assumption behind it: the first child this archive had FOUND was not necessarily his FIRST child. The years 1850-1855 are unread, and a son Giuseppe in one of them would restore the custom exactly. Recorded as a candidate: ORAZIO ARENA b. 14 DECEMBER 1821, son of Giuseppe Arena and a Teresa. FURTHER EVIDENCE, BOTH WAYS: Orazio's earliest known child is a DAUGHTER, Teresa, born 17 October 1853. Custom names the first daughter for her paternal grandmother, and act 10 of 1821 makes Orazio's mother a Teresa -- which SUPPORTS the 1821 candidate. But that same act makes his father a Giuseppe, and Orazio's first son is Domenico, with 1852-1855 now read and no earlier son. The two halves disagree and the archive is not picking one.

rows.recordSays: SUPERSEDED BY THE MARRIAGE ACT, and kept because the reasoning is worth reading. His parents are FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA, a sailor, and SERAFINA ARLOTTA. The proof is not the 1861 act alone but a SIBLING PAIR: act 45 of 1860 gives Francesco Antonio and Serafina a son GIUSEPPE, and act 228 of 1861 gives them a son ROCCO, twenty-one months apart. The tree gives Orazio Arena exactly two children and they are ROCCO and GUISEPPE -- the same pair, in the same order, on the wrong father. Meanwhile Orazio Arena and Giovanna Zirilli are documented across four years (1856, 1858, 1859, 1860) with children Domenico, Domenico and Maria Annunziata, and NEITHER a Rocco nor a Giuseppe ever appears. This was the case BEFORE act 63 of 1888 was found. It was built on a sibling pair and four years of negative sweeps, and it was right -- which is the point of keeping it.

rows.kind: a document against a document — a surname in dispute
rows.treeSays: Not in the tree; this archive publishes her as ANNA FAMA
rows.recordSays: TWO RECORDS, TWO SURNAMES, AND NEITHER IS THE ORIGINAL. Domenico Ventrice's wife is named twice in this archive and not the same way. The CHANCERY'S CERTIFIED COPY OF 1849, made thirty-four years after his death and filed in his granddaughter's marriage bundle at Briatico, calls her ANNA FAMA. His son's own marriage act -- ZAMBRONE, 2 MARCH 1824, written in the town where Domenico died and only nine years after he died, from the groom's own statement -- calls her «LA FU ANNA MAROPOLI». THE 1824 ACT IS PREFERRED, for three reasons: it is nearer the event by twenty-five years, it was written in the right comune, and THE SAME 1849 COPY HAS ALREADY BEEN CAUGHT GETTING SOMETHING WRONG -- it crams two ages into one clause and this archive first read Domenico as fifty when he was fifty-eight. BUT NEITHER IS THE ACT ITSELF. THE VOLUME HAS NOW BEEN OPENED AND THE ORIGINAL IS NOT THERE. Zambrone's death register runs 1811, then 1812 ending with its own Tavola, then a title page -- and then 1822. THE YEARS 1813 TO 1821 ARE PHYSICALLY ABSENT and Domenico died in January 1815. SO THIS CANNOT BE SETTLED FROM ZAMBRONE'S OWN REGISTER. ONE THING DID CHANGE, AND IN MAROPOLI'S FAVOUR: the 1822 death Tavola of the same volume names a «fu Franc.co e Dom.ca MAROPOLI» as the parents of a Francesca Pungitori. AND IT IS NOT AN ISOLATED INSTANCE. Sweeping the death Tavole of 1822, 1823 and 1824 turns up MAROPOLI TWICE: as a parent's surname in 1822, and as GIUSEPPE MAROPOLI himself, an infant dead on 23 March 1824, son of Antonio and Marianna Colia. TWO INDEPENDENT ATTESTATIONS INSIDE TWO YEARS. So the reading «della fu Anna Maropoli» no longer needs defending AS A READING. What stays open is only which of two documents is right -- and that cannot be decided until Domenico Ventrice's own act is found, which needs the second copy of a register whose comune copy is missing these years. Work list row 59.
rows.source: Zambrone, Matrimoni 1824 atto 2 and Morti 1822 Tavola; against Briatico, Matrimoni 1849, atto 1 (processetti)

(1) ANNA ARLOTTA, died 16 March 1915: «Padre GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, Madre MARIA COSTA, Coniuge ANTONINO COSTA» -- and Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa are SERAFINA ARLOTTA'S OWN PARENTS, so Anna and Serafina were sisters. (3) GENEROSA COSTA, died 6 June 1916: «Padre ANTONINO COSTA, Madre ANNA ARLOTTA» -- her own death act naming that same couple as her parents. rows.who: Generosa Costa × the second Generosa Costa
rows.recordSays: THERE ARE TWO AND THEY MUST NEVER BE MERGED. (1) GENEROSA COSTA, born about 1868, a filatrice, daughter of ANTONINO COSTA and ANNA ARLOTTA, married ROCCO ARENA at Scilla in December 1888, died at Scilla 6 JUNE 1916. She is on this archive's spine -- Anna Arena's mother. (2) A second GENEROSA COSTA, wife of PASQUALE DONATO, who died 20 April 1937; Pasquale is a son of DOMENICO DONATO and NUNZIATA SOFI, which makes him MICHELE DONATO'S BROTHER. So the two women sit one in each of this archive's two Scilla lines, the Arena and the Donato, and a tree that meets both will be tempted to fuse them. THE SEPARATION IS EVIDENCED, not assumed: the first was already dead in 1916, twenty-one years before the second's husband died, and their parents differ. COSTA AT SCILLA IS NOT A SMALL NAME -- the name index holds seventy-six Costa records and eighteen Costa deaths, including a THIRD Generosa in the previous generation, GENEROSA POLISTENA, for whom Rocco's wife was very likely named.

groups.kind: Two men of one name — A GUARD, NOT A FINDING

rows.kind: Two men of one name — A GUARD, NOT A FINDING
rows.who: Antonio Arena × the other Antonio Arena
rows.treeSays: One Antonio Arena married to a Serafina
rows.recordSays: THERE ARE TWO AND THE WIVES SHARE A GIVEN NAME. (1) FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA, b. 25 November 1819, m. SERAFINA ARLOTTA at Scilla on 7 February 1851, d. 29 August 1901 at Via Grotte 2. This archive's direct line. THE REGISTERS DROP HIS FIRST NAME CONSTANTLY -- the acts of 1853, 1854 and 1861 call him plain ANTONIO, and so does his son Giovanni's death act of 1936 -- so he is ROUTINELY INDEXED AS «Antonio Arena, husband of Serafina». (2) ANTONIO ARENA, husband of SERAFINA DE LUCA, a proprietario, both dead by August 1895 when their son ORAZIO ARENA died at sixty-five; three more of their children are in the death index -- GRAZIA (d. 14 February 1913), ANNA (d. 8 March 1917, wife of Rocco Paladino) and ANNUNZIATA (d. 12 April 1919). SAME GIVEN NAME, SAME WIFE'S GIVEN NAME, SAME TOWN, SAME DECADES. Anyone sweeping «Antonio Arena + Serafina» merges two families. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE WIFE'S SURNAME -- ARLOTTA or DE LUCA -- and it must be read every single time, never inferred. THE SECOND ONE IS ALREADY A TRAP THIS ARCHIVE HAS SPRUNG: the Orazio Arena who died in 1895 was taken for the tree's Orazio Arena, the supposed father of Rocco, and he is not -- he is Antonio and Serafina DE LUCA's son. Different wife, different parents, different family.

NAA: D4028 item 9209609 is ALSO CRUPI ANTONIO, born SERRATA, arrived MELBOURNE 20 October 1926 -- Serrata is in Calabria, six hundred kilometres from Piedimonte, and he is nobody here. groups.kind: Age — two of his own declarations, eleven years apart

rows.kind: Age — two of his own declarations, eleven years apart
rows.treeSays: Born about 1779, from being seventy-five in April 1854
rows.recordSays: HIS DAUGHTER'S BIRTH ACT MAKES HIM FORTY IN JUNE 1830, so born about 1790 -- ELEVEN YEARS LATER. Both figures are his own, given in person: in 1830 he declares Serafina's birth as her father, in 1854 he declares his grandson Giovanni's birth and is entered as «figlio del fu Domenico, di anni settantacinque, marinaro». Both call him marinaro; the 1830 act calls him «Sig.». NOT RESOLVED HERE, AND NOT AVERAGED. Either one declared age is badly out -- which this register does often enough -- or there are two Giovanni Arlotta and the 1854 declarant is not Serafina's father, which would cost this archive the Domenico Arlotta generation. THE TEST is his own marriage act to Maria Costa, before 1830, in the processetti of 1824-1827 or 1828-1831, which would give his age a third time and name his parents.

groups.kind: A lead, not a finding

rows.recordSays: A DOMENICO COSTA, COMMERCIANTE REGNICOLO, DI ANNI QUARANTASEI, stood as first witness at Serafina Arlotta's registration in June 1830 -- and the act says the witnesses were PRODUCED BY GIOVANNI ARLOTTA himself, which at Scilla means family. Forty-six in 1830 is a birth about 1784, which makes him twenty-three when Maria Costa was born about 1807. A father-in-law at his granddaughter's registration is the ordinary reading. IT IS A READING. Costa is one of the commonest surnames in the town -- seventy-six in the death index alone -- and this archive has already met a Domenica Costa, a Maria Costa, a Generosa Costa twice over and an Antonino Costa in four different households. The test is Giovanni Arlotta's marriage act, which names the bride's father outright.

groups.kind: All four alive — inferred in the morning, CONFIRMED in the afternoon

rows.kind: All four alive — inferred in the morning, CONFIRMED in the afternoon
rows.who: Filippo Arena, Domenica Costa, Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa
rows.treeSays: No date of any kind for three of the four
rows.recordSays: THEY WERE ALL FOUR ALIVE ON 7 FEBRUARY 1851 -- read from an absence, and graded accordingly. The marriage processetti of Francesco Arena and Serafina Arlotta run to FOUR SHEETS: the two birth acts, the notification without opposition, and the certificate of the canonical celebration. NO DEATH ACT OF ANY PARENT IS BOUND IN. The same office, in fascicolo 3 of the same year, bound in «Atto di morte del padre e dell'avo paterno dello Sposo» -- so it did include them when a parent or grandparent was dead. CAVEAT: Serafina was twenty and needed parental consent, and no consent sheet is listed either, so consent was given in person rather than on paper; an argument from a four-line index is weaker than an act, and this is graded as inferred for that reason. UPGRADED THE SAME DAY, AND BY A POSITIVE READING RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE. The ANNUAL MARRIAGE TAVOLA for 1851 names both spouses' parents AND MARKS THE DEAD WITH «FU» -- the 1828 Tavola writes Giovanni Arlotta's father as «FU Dom.co» beside his living mother «Barbaro Anna», and «fu» appears on this very page of 1851 in other entries. ENTRY 1 OF THE 1851 TAVOLA IS «ARENA FRANCESCO e ARLOTTA SERAFINA», and its parents are written «FILIPPO, e COSTA DOMENICA» and «GIOVANNI e COSTA MARIA» -- NEITHER WITH «FU». So all four were living when their children married, and this is no longer an argument from a four-line index.
rows.source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1849-1852, fascicolo 13 of 1851, against fascicolo 3 of 1851; Scilla, Matrimoni 1851, Tavola annuale, entry 1, against the same page's «fu» entries

groups.kind: Internment — a third man

rows.treeSays: Nothing but a Queensland death registration
rows.recordSays: INTERNED. His aliens registration card is stamped LOVEDAY 35924 on the front, and the CHANGE OF ADDRESS panel on the reverse records him moved «ex Gay[thorne] to 14A» on 16 MARCH 1943 and «Released and returned to Queensland» on 22 OCTOBER 1943. THAT IS THREE MEN IN THIS FAMILY INTERNED IN THE SAME EIGHTEEN MONTHS: ROSARIO MAZZA, who married Angela Crupi; MARIO CRUPI, at Loveday 18 August 1942 to 30 December 1943; and now ANTONINO CRUPI, her other brother. The internment of Italian-Australians was not a thing that happened to one member of this family. AND THE CENSOR PRESERVED A SENTENCE OF HIS. The card carries a mail extract dated 2 APRIL 1943, from a letter to his wife in Queensland: «... Our freedom will come soon and we shall always cry Vive Italia.» It is the only sentence in this archive spoken by Antonino Crupi, and it exists because an official copied it out as evidence against him.
rows.source: NAA: D4028, CRUPI ANTONIO (item 9209610), both sides

rows.recordSays: BOTH ON THE OTRANTO, INTO BRISBANE ON 19 AUGUST 1930. Antonino's own card gives his ENTRY as 2 SEPTEMBER 1930, a fortnight after the ship docked -- the same split between a ship's arrival and a man's registered entry already recorded for the passenger index. groups.kind: Identification — the roll could not settle it and a naturalisation did

rows.kind: Identification — the roll could not settle it and a naturalisation did
rows.treeSays: Two Antonio Crupi on the 1959 Queensland roll and no way to choose
rows.recordSays: HE IS THE TULLY MAN. NAA: A714 57/18792 records «CRUPI, Antonio; naturalised 7 NOVEMBER 1946; place of birth PIEDIMONTE, Italy; year of birth 1907; PLACE OF RESIDENCE: TULLY, QLD; [W] CRUPI, NELLIE». Piedimonte and 1907 tie it to the aliens card of Angela Crupi's brother; TULLY and NELLIE tie it to the 1959 electoral roll, where an ANTONIO CRUPI, cane farmer, shares DEAN STREET, TULLY with a NELLIE CRUPI. The other Antonio Crupi of that roll, a farmer at SILKWOOD EAST in the Innisfail sub-district, is a different man. THE ROW NAMED ITS OWN TEST -- «a wife to match against Nellie Crupi» -- and a document found while reading his brother's aliens card supplied it. Nothing here rests on the roll's ordering, which this archive has already been burned by once. AND HE MOVED. The aliens card of October 1939 gives him at INGHAM, a boot repairer; by 1946 he is a cane farmer at Tully, where Pietro and Mario also were. ONE THING TIDIED. The Queensland marriage of an Antonino Crupi on 24 AUGUST 1940 sat awkwardly against a card registered in October 1939 that already says MARRIED. The card carries annotations from 1943, so «married» was very probably written on it after the fact; the 1940 marriage is the likelier date and is very likely to Nellie. Stated as the reading it is.
rows.source: NAA: A714 57/18792; NAA: D4028 CRUPI ANTONIO (item 9209610); Australia Electoral Rolls 1959, Herbert, Tully sub-district

groups.kind: Port — the ship's first landfall is not where he got off

rows.kind: Port — the ship's first landfall is not where he got off
rows.recordSays: HE GOT OFF AT BRISBANE, ON 21 OCTOBER 1957. NAA: BP25/1, ITALIAN PROSTAMO F -- the BRISBANE aliens registration series -- reads «Prostamo, Francesco - Nationality: Italian - arrived BRISBANE on the T/v ROMA 21 OCTOBER 1957». BOTH DATES ARE TRUE AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS: 10 October is when the ROMA first touched Australia at Fremantle, which is what the passenger index records; 21 October is when this man walked down the gangway, eleven days and three ports later. THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because the family settled in Queensland and the Brisbane series is where he registered. The same correction applies to FRANCESCA PROSTAMO, who travelled with him: NAA: BP25/1, ITALIAN TRUNGADI F, same ship, same 21 October, same port. This is the third time this archive has met the pattern -- it was proved on a K269 manifest where an unlabelled letter column turned out to be the port of debarkation.
rows.source: NAA: BP25/1, ITALIAN PROSTAMO F (item 5067016) and ITALIAN TRUNGADI F (item 5080545)

groups.kind: A married surname, not a second woman

rows.kind: A married surname, not a second woman
rows.treeSays: Francesco Prostamo's daughter, born 1945 at Briatico, twelve on the voyage
rows.recordSays: THE NATIONAL ARCHIVES CATALOGUES HER AS «TRUNGADI [nee PROSTAMO], FRANCESCA». That is her Brisbane aliens registration, same ship and same day as her father. A TWELVE-YEAR-OLD IS NOT «NEE» ANYTHING, and the manifest -- read in the original -- gives her age as twelve and her birth as 1945 at Briatico. The reading that fits both is that the registration CARD was annotated with her married name years after 1957 and the catalogue transcribed the card's final state, which is exactly what an aliens card is for. SO TRUNGADI IS A SURNAME TO GO LOOKING FOR -- a Queensland marriage, a later address -- AND NOT A SECOND WOMAN TO ADD. Recorded as a lead.

groups.kind: Marriage — undocumented until now

rows.treeSays: Their marriage is not documented anywhere in this archive
rows.recordSays: A COMMONWEALTH FILE NAMES THEM AS HUSBAND AND WIFE. NAA: J25 1971/3900, held at Brisbane, 1953-1971: «ARENA, ROCCO; WIFE ANGELINA [OR ANGELA] [NEE POLISTENA]». J25 is the Queensland immigration and naturalisation correspondence series, and its file titles name a couple together with the WIFE'S MAIDEN NAME -- which is exactly what was missing. IT DOES NOT DATE THE MARRIAGE. What it does is turn «undocumented» into «documented as a fact, undated», and name the file that may date it. The file is «not yet examined», which means nobody has ever asked; an access examination is free and takes about ninety days. Michael's grandparents on the Arena side.

groups.kind: A second migration, twenty years and half a world apart

rows.kind: A second migration, twenty years and half a world apart
rows.treeSays: One crossing: Palermo to New Orleans, 1908
rows.recordSays: HE MAY HAVE GONE TO AUSTRALIA TOO. NAA: BP9/3, ITALIAN POLISTENA G -- the Brisbane aliens register -- reads «Polistena, GIOVANNI BORN 1883 - nationality Italian - arrived in BRISBANE on the ORMONDE 21 FEBRUARY 1928». This archive's Giovanni Polistena was born at Scilla in 1883 (act 206), sailed from PALERMO to NEW ORLEANS on the LIGURIA in February 1908 on the line immediately after Michele Donato, married Michele's daughter Nunziata about 1916, and named a daughter Santa at Scilla in 1920. A crossing to Brisbane in 1928 sits after all of that and would explain how this family reached Queensland at all. THE YEAR OF BIRTH MATCHES EXACTLY AND THE PORT IS THE RIGHT ONE. IT IS STILL A CANDIDATE: the register entry carries no parents and no birthplace, and POLISTENA is a comune in Reggio Calabria as well as a surname, so the name alone proves nothing. The test is the item itself, or any Queensland record placing him there in the 1930s.

groups.kind: Two families, six marriages

rows.treeSays: Two Donato-Polistena marriages, a generation apart
rows.recordSays: SIX, ACROSS TWO COUNTRIES. Four at Scilla, from the death index: Maria Donato x Giuseppe Polistina (she d. 1911); Raffaele Polistena x Teresa Donato, three of whose children die there; Giovanni Polistena x Annunziata Donato; and Nunziata Donato x Giovanni Polistena about 1916. TWO MORE IN QUEENSLAND, from the National Archives: NAA J25 1967/9873, «Polistena, Giuseppe; wife MARIA MADDALENA [nee DONATO]», and NAA J25 1970/3023, «DONATO, CONCETTA [nee POLISTENA]». TWO FAMILIES THAT INTERMARRY SIX TIMES OVER TWO GENERATIONS AND TWO HEMISPHERES ARE NOT TWO FAMILIES WHO HAPPENED TO MEET. They were one neighbourhood at Scilla -- Via Grotte -- and they were still one neighbourhood in Brisbane.
rows.source: Antenati name index, Scilla; NAA: J25 1967/9873 and 1970/3023

groups.kind: A surname that is also a town — A GUARD

rows.kind: A surname that is also a town — A GUARD

A name search on POLISTENA in the National Archives returns four A714 naturalisations for men called OLIMPIO, MARFEA, FOGLIADORO and PALESTRI whose PLACE OF BIRTH is Polistena, and three A7919 prisoner-of-war files -- SAVARESE, ROSSI, BOTTIGLIERI -- for men born there and captured in Africa. rows.treeSays: An index that gives a name and a number
rows.recordSays: IT GIVES FOUR PARENTS AND TELLS YOU WHICH OF THEM WERE DEAD. Scilla's «TAVOLA annuale alfabetica dei Matrimonj» carries the columns Num. d'ordine | Cognomi e Nomi degli Sposi | Patria | Professione | COGNOMI E NOMI DE' GENITORI | Giorno della Celebrazione -- and the parents column uses the Italian convention: «FU X» where the parent is dead, a bare forename where the parent is living. The 1828 Tavola writes Giovanni Arlotta as son of «FU Dom.co e Barbaro Anna»: father dead, mother alive, in four words. ONE INDEX OPENING THEREFORE DATES THE LIFE STATUS OF FOUR PEOPLE AT A SINGLE MOMENT, without opening an act. That is a better instrument than this archive has been treating it as, and it applies to every year of the restaurazione series. CAVEAT: the date column is the CHURCH celebration, not the civil act -- in 1828 the Tavola says 7 September where the civil promise was 30 August -- so an act number and a Tavola date will not agree, and neither is wrong.

rows.kind: A structural finding about the thinnest quarter
rows.treeSays: One of this archive's four Scilla families
rows.recordSays: THEY ARE BARELY IN THE BIRTH REGISTERS OF THE 1830s. Three complete annual P sections -- 1834, 1835 and 1836 -- cover 629 BIRTHS AND HOLD EXACTLY ONE POLISTENA. The P section at Scilla in those years is Paladino, Pirrotta, Patafio, Papalia, Pizzarello, Parisi, Piria. THE POLISTENA ARE NOT AN OLD SCILLA SURNAME AT THAT DATE. WHICH MAY BE WHY THIS QUARTER STOPS. The Polistena line reaches Camillo Antonio, born about 1835, and above him only his parents' names off a death act. If the family came INTO Scilla rather than being of it, the generation above will be in another comune's registers -- and POLISTENA IS ITSELF A COMUNE in the province of Reggio Calabria, seventy kilometres away, which is exactly where a surname like that comes from. Recorded as a reading of an absence, not a finding, and the test is whether Camillo Antonio's birth act exists at Scilla at all.
rows.source: Scilla, Nati 1834, 1835 and 1836, Tavole annuali — complete P sections

groups.kind: A lead with the wrong surname on it — OPENED, AND THE INDEX WAS THE LIAR

rows.kind: A lead with the wrong surname on it — OPENED, AND THE INDEX WAS THE LIAR
rows.treeSays: Camillo Antonio Polistena has no documented siblings
rows.recordSays: «POLISTINA ANNUNZIATA, DI GIUSEPPE E MARTELLO ANNA» -- entry 191 of the 1836 Scilla birth Tavola, born 2 DECEMBER 1836, and the ONLY Polistena birth in three years of that register. THE GIVEN NAMES ARE RIGHT AND THE SURNAME IS NOT. Camillo Antonio Polistena's death act of 1924 gives his parents as GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO. Here the mother is ANNA MARTELLO. THREE READINGS AND NO DECISION: the Tavola is wrong; the death act is wrong; or these are two different couples who each happen to pair a Giuseppe with an Anna. TWO THINGS MAKE THE FIRST WORTH TESTING. The Tavola is an INDEX, and this archive has already been caught by one -- the 1854 index that called Serafina Arlotta «Rosa» and briefly turned a brother into a cousin. AND FOUR ENTRIES EARLIER, at 168, stands «PONTILLO GIOVANNI, di Giuseppe e Paladino Giuseppa» -- a Pontillo household with a Giuseppe at its head, in the same section of the same page. A clerk copying down that column had both surnames under his hand. ACT 191 OF 1836 SETTLES IT AND IS THREE IMAGES AWAY. OPENED THE SAME HOUR. ACT 204 OF 1836 -- not 191; the Tavola's «Num. d'ordine» is an index row and this index carries NO act number at all. Scilla, 2 DECEMBER 1836: the midwife TERESA ARENA, forty-four, declared a girl born that morning at eight to ANNA PONTILLO, THIRTY-FIVE, lawful wife of GIUSEPPE POLISTINA, THIRTY-EIGHT, MARINARO, and named ANNUNZIATA POLISTINA. THE MOTHER IS PONTILLO. The Tavola's «Martello» is wrong, the death act of 1924 is right, and ANNUNZIATA IS CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA'S SISTER -- the first sibling he has ever had here. The guess about WHY the index erred also held: four entries earlier in the same P section stands «Pontillo Giovanni, di Giuseppe e Paladino Giuseppa».
rows.source: Scilla, Nati 1836, Tavola annuale, entry 191; Scilla, Nati 1836 atto 204, read in the original

rows.recordSays: IT DOES NOT, IN 1836. That Tavola's columns are Num. d'ordine | Cognomi e Nomi dei Nati | Cognomi e Nomi dei Genitori | GIORNO DELLA NASCITA -- and THERE IS NO ACT-NUMBER COLUMN. The «Num. d'ordine» is the INDEX ROW, running 1 to 222 across the alphabet. Entry 191 is a Polistina; ACT 191 of the register is a SQUILLACI birth at Solano on 9 November. THE ONLY KEY FROM THIS INDEX INTO THIS REGISTER IS THE DATE OF BIRTH, and the acts run in date order -- which found act 204 in two probes. This is the Briatico 1828 trap in a harder form: there the index ran one behind the register, here it does not point at the register at all.

groups.kind: Age — wrong by at least six years, and eleven years prove it

rows.kind: Age — wrong by at least six years, and eleven years prove it
rows.treeSays: Born about 1835, from being forty-eight in September 1883
rows.recordSays: HE IS NOT IN THE SCILLA BIRTH REGISTER FOR 1833, 1834, 1835, 1836, 1837 OR 1838. Six consecutive complete P sections. AND HIS PARENTS ARE IN TWO OF THEM: GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO have a son ROCCO on 13 DECEMBER 1833 and a daughter ANNUNZIATA on 2 DECEMBER 1836. THE THREE YEARS BETWEEN HOLD NO POLISTENA BIRTH AT ALL, and they are not thin years -- 201, 206 and 222 births. A child born to this couple about 1835 is simply not there. SO «FORTY-EIGHT» IN SEPTEMBER 1883 IS OUT BY AT LEAST TWO YEARS, and he was born BEFORE 1833 or AFTER 1838. Declared ages in this register are routinely a year out; this one is worse. THE SEARCH MOVES TO 1830-1832 AND 1839-1840, and it should not stop at the first year that fits. EXTENDED TO ELEVEN YEARS, 1830-1840, AND THE DIRECTION IS NOW FIXED. His parents' children come in DECEMBER 1833, DECEMBER 1836 and JANUARY 1840 -- three years apart, twice, with 1830, 1831 and 1832 read and empty of them. SO ROCCO IS THE ELDEST AND CAMILLO ANTONIO CANNOT BE EARLIER; he must be 1841 OR LATER, and «forty-eight» in September 1883 is wrong by at least SIX years. THE NAMING CUSTOM AGREES: a first son takes the father's father's name, making Giuseppe's father a ROCCO POLISTENA, and a later son takes the mother's father's -- which would make CAMILLO ANTONIO the namesake of a CAMILLO PONTILLO. Anna Pontillo was about thirty-five in 1836 and could bear to about 1846, so the window is 1841-1848.
rows.source: Scilla, Nati 1830-1840, Tavole annuali — eleven complete P sections

groups.kind: A second Polistena household — A GUARD

rows.kind: A second Polistena household — A GUARD
rows.recordSays: THERE ARE AT LEAST TWO. The 1839 birth Tavola, entry 153, gives «POLISTINA MARIA -- FRANCESCO e LONGARDO GIUSEPPA -- 30 Maggio». That is not GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO, this archive's couple, and the child is not a sibling of Camillo Antonio. IT MATTERS BECAUSE THE SURNAME IS SO RARE HERE. Seven consecutive years of the Scilla birth register -- 1833 to 1839, about 1,450 births -- hold exactly FOUR Polistena, and three of them belong to these two couples. With a surname that scarce, the temptation to join any two bearers is strong and it should be resisted: the discriminator is the MOTHER, and here it is Longardo against Pontillo. NOTED AND NOT CONCLUDED FROM: LONGARDO is the surname of NATALINA LONGORDO, mother of the Filippo Arena who died at Scilla in 1915 and who was briefly taken for Rocco Arena's brother. The two spellings are one Scilla surname. AND THEY WERE THERE BEFORE THIS ARCHIVE'S COUPLE. The 1832 Tavola, entry 152, gives «POLISTINA DOMENICA -- FRANCESCO e LONGORDO GIUSEPPA -- 17 Dicembre». So Francesco and Giuseppa had a daughter in December 1832 and another in May 1839, while Giuseppe and Anna Pontillo had theirs in December 1833 and December 1836. TWO HOUSEHOLDS RUNNING IN PARALLEL FOR EIGHT YEARS, and between them they account for EVERY Polistena birth at Scilla in that time -- five in about 1,630 births.

SHE IS THE THIRD SIBLING FOUND TODAY, after Rocco (13 December 1833) and Annunziata (2 December 1836). AND THE THREE OF THEM GIVE THE FAMILY A SHAPE. Children in December 1833, December 1836 and January 1840 -- THREE YEARS APART, TWICE -- with 1830, 1831, 1832, 1834, 1835, 1837, 1838 and 1839 all read and holding no child of theirs. That is a regular household, and it means Rocco is the eldest and Camillo Antonio is younger than all three.

groups.kind: Three Polistena households, not one — THE MAP

rows.kind: Three Polistena households, not one — THE MAP
rows.treeSays: A surname with one household behind it
rows.recordSays: THREE, AND ELEVEN YEARS OF THE BIRTH REGISTER NAME ALL OF THEM. GIUSEPPE POLISTENA x ANNA PONTILLO -- this archive's -- with Rocco (1833), Annunziata (1836) and Fortunata (1840). FRANCESCO POLISTINA x GIUSEPPA LONGARDO, with Salvadore (1830), Domenica (1832) and Maria (1839). LUIGI POLISTINA x MARIANNA (or GIOVANNA) BAVIERA, with Antonino (1830) and Francesco Antonio (1831). EIGHT BIRTHS IN ABOUT 2,100. The surname is scarce enough that any two bearers look related and rare enough that the temptation to join them is strong. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE MOTHER, every time: Pontillo, Longardo, Baviera. NOTE ONE TRAP IN PARTICULAR: Luigi's son born 21 June 1831 is called FRANCESCO ANTONIO POLISTINA. That is one word away from CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA, in the right town in the right decade, and it is a different child of different parents. It would be very easy to seize on.

groups.kind: A Giuseppe and an Anna Pontillo who are NOT these two — A GUARD

rows.kind: A Giuseppe and an Anna Pontillo who are NOT these two — A GUARD
rows.treeSays: One couple at Scilla answering to «Giuseppe e Anna Pontillo»

This archive's couple are GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO, whose children appear in the same register in 1833, 1836 and 1840. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY COLLISION: the way this archive has been searching these Tavole is by READING THE PARENTS COLUMN for «Giuseppe e Pontillo Anna». That method walks straight into this entry and cannot tell the difference, because the thing that separates them is the CHILD'S SURNAME -- the column a parent-scan skips. It is written down so that the next person reading these pages checks the first column before celebrating.

groups.kind: Method — a birth act is not only a birth

rows.kind: Method — a birth act is not only a birth
rows.treeSays: A birth act gives a date, a house and two parents
rows.recordSays: IT ALSO CARRIES MARGINAL ANNOTATIONS ADDED DECADES LATER, and this archive has read a dozen of these acts without once looking at the margin. Scilla atto 174 of 1833 -- Rocco Polistina's birth -- has written down its left edge: «L'anno 1869, il giorno 12 Luglio ... HA CONTRATTO MATRIMONIO IN QUESTO COMUNE CON COLORINA BRI[...]», signed by the Uffiziale and dated from Reggio on 26 August 1869. THIRTY-SIX YEARS AFTER THE BIRTH, IN A DIFFERENT HAND. THE PRINTED FORM ASKS FOR IT: the left column is headed «MARGINE per scriversi alcune notizie riguardanti gli atti di nascita», and the right «INDICAZIONE del giorno in cui è stato amministrato il Sagramento del Battesimo». One is the baptism, which this archive does read; the other is everything that happened to the person afterwards, which it does not. WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT: go back to the margins of the acts already read -- Francesco Antonio Arena 1819 atto 186, Serafina Arlotta 1830 atto 89, Rocco Arena 1861 atto 228, the four 1852-1860 Arena births -- and look. A marriage annotation would date a wedding without a marriage register at all.

groups.kind: Method, calibrated — what a blank margin is and is not worth

rows.kind: Method, calibrated — what a blank margin is and is not worth
rows.treeSays: A birth act's margin may carry a later marriage
rows.recordSays: THREE MARGINS NOW READ, AND THE RULE IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKED. ROCCO POLISTINA, born 1833, married AT SCILLA on 12 July 1869: HIS MARGIN CARRIES IT, written by the same office, signed, and dated from Reggio six weeks later. SERAFINA ARLOTTA, born 1830, married at Scilla on 7 February 1851: HER MARGIN IS EMPTY. FILIPPO ARENA, born 1852, who would have married after 1866 if he married at Scilla: HIS MARGIN IS EMPTY. THE READING THAT FITS ALL THREE is that the annotation is an ITALIAN-ERA administrative habit -- it appears on a marriage of 1869 and not on one of 1851 -- and that it is written only when the later act is registered in the SAME COMUNE, since the note itself says «ha contratto matrimonio IN QUESTO COMUNE». SO A BLANK MARGIN IS WEAK EVIDENCE AND MUST NOT BE READ AS «HE NEVER MARRIED». For a pre-1866 marriage it means nothing at all. For a post-1866 one it is consistent with a marriage ELSEWHERE, which for Filippo Arena is exactly the reading the rest of the evidence already supports -- he is absent from Scilla's death index from 1889 to 1943 and from the name index of 1910-1943. ONE MORE STRAW ON THE PILE THAT HE LEFT, and not a proof of anything.
rows.source: Scilla, Nati 1833 atto 174; Nati 1830 atto 89; Nati 1852 atto 48

groups.kind: Declared ages — the extreme case, kept as a warning

rows.who: Francesco Antonio Arena and Serafina Arlotta
rows.treeSays: Declared ages in this register are usually a year or two out
rows.recordSays: IN ATTO 48 OF 1852 THEY ARE FOUR AND SEVEN YEARS OUT, IN THE SAME LINE. He is entered as THIRTY-SIX and was thirty-two; she as TWENTY-EIGHT and was twenty-one -- and she had married twelve months earlier on an act that makes her twenty. TWO YEARS LATER, in atto 76 of 1854, the same couple are THIRTY-FOUR and TWENTY-TWO, which fits their birth acts. The register did not age them; a clerk guessed, and guessed badly. THIS IS THE ACT TO POINT AT whenever a declared age is about to be used to identify somebody. It is also why Camillo Antonio Polistena's «forty-eight» has now been shown wrong by at least six years without anything being wrong with the man.

groups.kind: A son who is a daughter — MY OWN ERROR, RETRACTED

rows.kind: A son who is a daughter — MY OWN ERROR, RETRACTED
rows.treeSays: DOMENICO ARENA b. 24 March 1853, one of Rocco Arena's three brothers
rows.recordSays: SHE IS DOMENICA ARENA AND SHE IS HIS SISTER. Scilla, atto 53 of 1853, read in the original: FRANCESCANTONIO ARENA presented «UNA FEMINA», declared «di dare alla FANCIULLA il nome di DOMENICA», and the Indicazione column records the baptism of DOMENICA ARENA on the same day. Three independent statements inside one act. HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, BECAUSE IT WILL HAPPEN AGAIN: she was taken from the ANNUAL TAVOLA, where a surname-ordered index line reading «Arena Domenica di Francescantonio e Arlotta Serafina» was read as Domenico. The Tavola was not wrong; the reading was, and NOBODY OPENED THE ACT for fourteen weeks. This archive's own caution says «read the act, not the index», and this is the fourth time that caution has been vindicated -- after the tavola numbers, the «Rosa» Arlotta of 1854, and the Mazza bride who was a Muzzi. WHAT IT CHANGES. Rocco Arena had TWO documented brothers, not three -- FILIPPO (1852) and GIUSEPPE (1860), plus GIOVANNI (1854) and himself. And row 146's «three brothers vanish after 1898» becomes TWO: a married daughter leaves the Arena surname and stops appearing under it, which is not a disappearance.

rows.kind: Margins — RETRACTED WITHIN THE HOUR: a blank means nothing after all
rows.treeSays: A blank margin is weak evidence
rows.recordSays: IT IS STRONGER THAN I ALLOWED AN HOUR AGO, BECAUSE THE CONTROL NOW EXISTS. The 1852 volume DOES carry marriage annotations: act 55 of 1852 has «Atto 18 Febbraio 1881 N. 11 -- SCARFONE ROCCO contrasse matrimonio in Scilla con VITA MARIA», written in the margin and dated from Reggio. The 1853 volume does it twice on one opening -- act 54 (a marriage of 20 December 1876) and act 55 («PALADINO SANTA contrasse matrimonio in Scilla», 8 September 1883). SO THE PRACTICE WAS APPLIED IN THESE VERY VOLUMES, AND FILIPPO ARENA'S MARGIN IS EMPTY. That is now evidence rather than nothing: HE DID NOT MARRY AT SCILLA. It still does not prove he never married -- a wedding in another comune would not be written back, and a clerk can miss one -- but set beside his absence from Scilla's death index 1889-1943 and from the name index of 1910-1943, it is a third silence pointing the same way. RETRACTED THE SAME AFTERNOON, AND BY A CASE THAT SETTLES IT. GIUSEPPE ARENA MARRIED MARIA MARTELLO AT SCILLA ON 12 SEPTEMBER 1885 -- act 73, read here in the original -- AND HIS OWN BIRTH ACT, NATI 1860 ATTO 45, HAS AN EMPTY ANNOTATION BOX. A man who demonstrably married at Scilla after 1866 was not annotated. THEREFORE A BLANK BOX IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT SOMEBODY DID NOT MARRY THERE, and the inference drawn against Filippo Arena is withdrawn in full. WHAT SURVIVES: a PRESENT annotation is worth having -- Rocco Polistina's 1869 marriage came free that way, and so did marriages of 1876, 1881 and 1883 on other acts. The annotation is a bonus when it is there and says NOTHING when it is not. NOTE ALSO THAT THE BOX MOVES. The 1852 and 1853 volumes use a left-hand column headed «MARGINE per scriversi alcune notizie riguardanti gli atti di Nascita»; the 1860 volume uses a right-hand box headed «MENZIONI prescritte dagli articoli 64, 65 e 106». Same purpose, opposite side of the page -- so «the margin is blank» must mean the right box was looked at.
rows.source: Scilla, Nati 1852 atti 48 and 55; Nati 1853 atti 54 and 55; Nati 1860 atto 45 against Matrimoni 1885 atto 73

rows.who: Luigi Carmelo Polistina and Annunziata Matra
rows.treeSays: Named only from a death act of 1933
rows.recordSays: THEY MARRIED AT SCILLA ON 23 NOVEMBER 1882, act 48. He was THIRTY, a MARINAIO, BORN AT SCILLA, son of RAFFAELE POLISTENA and TERESA DONATO -- both living. She was a FILATRICE, born at Scilla, daughter of GIACOMO MATRA, living, and the late CONCETTA LEOTTA. THE ACT AND THE NAME INDEX AGREE PERFECTLY ACROSS FIFTY-ONE YEARS: «Luigi Polistena, died 8 December 1933 -- Padre Raffaele, Madre Teresa Donato, Coniuge Annunziata Matra.» AND IT GIVES RAFFAELE POLISTENA AND TERESA DONATO THEIR FIRST DATE OF ANY KIND -- both alive in November 1882 -- and makes THEIR marriage a named target, before about 1852. That is the Donato-Polistena join one generation further back than row 138 had it.

groups.kind: Age — nine years out, and it sent the whole search the wrong way

rows.kind: Age — nine years out, and it sent the whole search the wrong way
rows.treeSays: Born about 1835, from being forty-eight on his son's birth act of September 1883
rows.recordSays: BORN ABOUT 1844. His own marriage act of 23 JANUARY 1881 makes him THIRTY-SIX -- so born between late January 1844 and late January 1845. The 1883 figure is NINE YEARS OUT, and it is the figure this archive built a sixteen-year sweep of the birth registers on. WHICH DECLARATION TO PREFER: THE MARRIAGE ACT. He appeared in person to marry, where age carried legal weight and the parish papers had been checked; the 1883 age was given by a man registering a newborn at nine in the evening. This archive has already ruled the same way for Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa. AND IT EXPLAINS THE SILENCE RATHER THAN DEEPENING IT. Eleven years of birth Tavole were read around 1835 because of the 1883 age. The answer was never in them. 1844 and 1845 ARE in the swept range -- but the 1844 reading covered only entries 127-138 without establishing where the P block ends, and 1845 is recorded as PARTIAL with seven of eighteen lines too faint. BOTH NEED GOING BACK TO, and that is now the shortest road left.
rows.source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1881 atto 4, against Nati 1883 atto 206

groups.kind: Death — a first bound for both of them

rows.kind: Death — a first bound for both of them
rows.treeSays: No death, no bound, for either
rows.recordSays: BOTH WERE DEAD BEFORE 23 JANUARY 1881. Their son's marriage act calls him «figlio del FU Giuseppe ... e della FU Anna Pontillo», each «residente in vita in Scilla» -- the formula for a parent who died in the comune. So: GIUSEPPE POLISTENA, born about 1798, alive at his daughter Fortunata's birth in January 1840, DEAD BY JANUARY 1881. ANNA PONTILLO, born about 1800, the same. Forty-one years of window, and it is the first bound either has ever had. IT ALSO CONFIRMS THE PARENTAGE FROM A SECOND DOCUMENT. Camillo Antonio's death act of 1924 named them; this act names them again, forty-three years earlier and from his own mouth. The identification no longer rests on one record.

rows.treeSays: Named as Camillo Antonio Polistena's wife; parents from her death act
rows.recordSays: TWENTY-SIX AND A FILATRICE at her marriage on 23 January 1881, so BORN ABOUT 1854, and NATA IN QUESTO COMUNE -- born at Scilla. Her parents are given as ANNUNZIATO, resident in this Comune, and ANGELA ZIRILLI, resident here -- BOTH LIVING in January 1881. THIS IS THE FOURTH RECORD TO CALL HER A ROMANO and the FIRST in which she is the subject rather than somebody's mother or wife. The family tree calls her «Giovanna Pontillo»; the register has now said Romano in her son's birth act of 1883, in a New Orleans manifest of 1908, in her own death act of 1930, and here in her own marriage act of 1881. The question is closed as firmly as it can be.

groups.kind: Birth — found, and my own partial reading is why it took so long

rows.kind: Birth — found, and my own partial reading is why it took so long
rows.treeSays: Born about 1835; not in sixteen years of the Scilla birth register
rows.recordSays: BORN AT SCILLA ON 21 SEPTEMBER 1844. The 1844 annual Tavola, entry 142: «Polistina Camillo -- Giuseppe e Pontillo Anna -- 21 Settembre». THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES EXACTLY. Born 21 September 1844, he is THIRTY-SIX YEARS AND FOUR MONTHS at his marriage on 23 January 1881, and the act says «di anni trentasei». At his son Giovanni's birth on 16 September 1883 he was THIRTY-EIGHT and eleven months, and that act says FORTY-EIGHT -- ten years wrong, and the figure this archive searched around. MY OWN READING IS WHY IT TOOK SIXTEEN YEARS OF SWEEPING. The 1844 P block was read earlier the same day, the crop stopped at entry 138, and the row recorded that the end of the block had not been established. HE IS AT 142. A PARTIAL READING WRITTEN DOWN AS A NEGATIVE IS THE SAME ERROR AS A 403 WRITTEN DOWN AS A NIL -- this archive has a rule about the second and needed one about the first.
rows.source: Scilla, Nati 1844, Tavola annuale, entry 142; against Matrimoni 1881 atto 4 and Nati 1883 atto 206

groups.kind: Birth act — read in the original, and the margin points at his marriage

rows.kind: Birth act — read in the original, and the margin points at his marriage
rows.treeSays: Born 21 September 1844, from the annual Tavola only
rows.recordSays: THE ACT IS SCILLA, NATI 1844, ATTO 137 -- not 142, which was the Tavola's row number. GIUSEPPE POLISTINA, fifty, MARINARO, presented a son born to ANNA PONTILLO, filatrice, his lawful wife, «NEL GIORNO VENTUNO CORRENTE MESE», and named him CAMILLO ANTONIO. The baptism column names CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTINA. THE GIVEN NAME IS SETTLED: the index says «Camillo», the act says «CAMILLO ANTONIO», and that is what every later record calls him. AND THE MARGIN CARRIES HIS MARRIAGE, annotated «Scilla 25 Gennaio 1881» -- two days after the wedding of 23 January 1881 in Matrimoni 1881 atto 4. The birth act and the marriage act point at each other across thirty-seven years, and the identification is now closed from both ends.

rows.kind: Marriage — found, and the wall this archive built was made of a wrong start year
rows.treeSays: Married before Scilla's civil registration and therefore lost to a parish register; «THE ARENA LINE STOPS HERE»
rows.recordSays: MARRIED AT SCILLA ON 12 NOVEMBER 1815, Matrimoni atto 29, and the act names BOTH SETS OF PARENTS. This archive wrote the wall itself: it searched 1816-1819 because it believed Scilla began in 1816, found nothing, and concluded the marriage was pre-civil. Scilla begins in 1809. Once the napoleonic volumes were opened the marriage was four years earlier, in an unindexed volume that fell to one montage pass. THE RETRACTION IS OF A CONCLUSION, NOT A READING -- every negative reported for 1810, 1811, 1812, 1816, 1817, 1818 and 1819 stands.

rows.treeSays: Born about 1792 or about 1787, depending which act was believed
rows.recordSays: BORN AT SCILLA ON 16 JUNE 1787 AND BAPTISED THE SAME DAY by the archpriest Giuseppe Ingigneri, with the name DOMINICA JOSEPHA. So her own marriage act was right -- twenty-eight in November 1815 -- and her husband's answer at their son's birth registration in 1819 was FIVE YEARS WRONG: she was thirty-two, not twenty-seven. This archive had recorded both figures and refused to choose; the baptism chooses.

groups.kind: Given name — corrected within the day

rows.kind: Given name — corrected within the day
rows.treeSays: Setteria Morabito, as this archive read the civil marriage act that morning
rows.recordSays: LITTERIA MORABITO. Her son's baptism extract, written in a clear Latin hand and copied into the same bundle, reads «ex Horatio Arena et LITTERIA MORABITO coniugibus». Litteria is a real name on this coast -- from the Madonna della Lettera, patroness of Messina across the strait -- and Setteria is not. THE RULE THIS PAYS FOR: where a marriage bundle survives, read the extracts before trusting a given name off the civil act; the parish copy is usually the better hand.

groups.kind: Generation nine, on the Scilla side, for the first time

rows.kind: Generation nine, on the Scilla side, for the first time
rows.treeSays: The Scilla lines stop at Filippo Arena, generation seven
rows.recordSays: GIUSEPPE COSTA AND GIACOMA TURCO, both dead before March 1790. Three documents stacked: the 1815 civil act named Domenica Costa's dead father; the marriage bundle copied his parish death act; and that act calls him «filius QUONDAM Josephi et Jacobae Turco». The single word «quondam» is what makes them generation nine and what dates them. Nothing further is reachable -- Scilla's civil registers begin nineteen years after their son died.

groups.kind: The parish books of Scilla existed in 1815 and were named

rows.kind: The parish books of Scilla existed in 1815 and were named
rows.treeSays: Row 158: pre-1809 Scilla is parish, and nothing is known of what survives
rows.recordSays: SOMETHING IS NOW KNOWN. The 1815 bundle quotes two books by name and cites the officials who held them: the «liber Baptizatorum» and the «liber Defunctorum» of the Matrice, kept by the archpriest D. GIUSEPPE INGIGNERI and searched by the economo curato LEONARDO CANTORE BANDIERA, who signed all three extracts. The baptism book was open at 1787 and 1793 and the death book at 1790, so both ran back at least to 1787. That is what to ask the Archivio Storico Diocesano at Reggio about -- named books, named custodians, named years -- rather than a general question about Scilla.

groups.kind: Wall — RETRACTED, and it was never a wall

rows.kind: Wall — RETRACTED, and it was never a wall
rows.treeSays: Published here since 15 September as one of this archive's four established walls: «his marriage to Domenica Costa is pre-1816, and Scilla's civil registration begins in 1816»
rows.recordSays: IT IS SCILLA, MATRIMONI 1815, ATTO 29, AND THE WALL HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM THE LIST. The wall's own evidence paragraph is the confession: it says the window was «four years wide -- between the first register and their son's birth in 1819 -- and ALL FOUR YEARS HAVE BEEN READ». All four were read, correctly, and the marriage was in the fifth. Scilla's registers begin in 1809. A wall built on a start year is only as good as the start year, and this one was checked against a belief instead of against the register index.
rows.source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1815 atto 29; Antenati register index for Scilla
